x.note: Type 2: first examination at diagnosis. Type 1: 5 years after onset. With mild or moderate retinopathy the interval is the NEAR end of ICO's range (12 and 6 months); the far end (24 and 12) applies only where a clinician has confirmed that control is at target, because ICO's schedule is stated for controlled diabetes and most patients with retinopathy here are above target. With no retinopathy the default is WHO's 24 months (D-DM-14). A blocking caveat acts by its direction. 'Masks' (undilated ophthalmoscopy, a calcified ankle-brachial index): a normal result is not trusted, an abnormal one stands. 'Manufactures' (fever or exercise before a urine albumin): an abnormal result is not trusted. 'Unpredictable': neither. In a diagnostic criteria set any blocking caveat also stops a positive, as the live catalog does. A value under a blocking caveat is never shown in a control band, is never the measure of a proposed target, and is not read by a treatment-review step. A caveat never suppresses an acute rule or a referral. The examination does not reset its screening interval.
